I am an old man now, 78 years, and my body is not what it was. My wife and I, just the two of us on these 3 mu. My son lives in the city. So I must be careful — I cannot do heavy work for many days, and I cannot afford to waste money on fertilizer I do not need. But I also cannot afford a bad harvest. At my age, a lost season is not something I recover from easily.

I have been doing wheat-maize rotation for more than 40 years on this land. I know this soil. Last year the wheat gave me about 450 jin per mu, the maize about 550 kg per mu. That is normal for our village. My neighbors get similar.

For wheat, I sow in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved variety seed — Jimai or Shimai, whatever the agro-shop in town has this year. The old varieties my father used are gone, nobody sells them anymore. At sowing I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (diammonium, 50 jin bag) per mu — that gives me about 9 kg of phosphorus and some nitrogen to start. Then in spring, around the green-up, I broadcast urea, maybe 30 jin per mu. That is what everyone does here. Potassium I add a little through the compound fertilizer but not much extra — our soil here has enough potassium, my neighbors do not add much either.

Wheat needs water. I irrigate from the well three times — before winter, at green-up in spring, and at grain filling. Pesticide I spray twice — once for aphids in spring, once for rust or powdery mildew if I see it. At my age I hire the neighbor's son with the sprayer for 20 yuan per mu, it is worth it.

For maize, I sow right after wheat harvest in June, no tillage, just direct seeding into the stubble — this is how we do it now, it saves time and the combine chopped the wheat straw already. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu variety. One bag compound fertilizer at sowing, then urea topdress at the big-trumpet stage — about 40 jin per mu because maize is a hungry crop. Irrigate twice if the rains are poor — tasseling and grain fill are the critical times. Spray once or twice for corn borer.

I will not change much from last year. At 78, I do what I know works.
